sentences.text: Caipirasuchus represents an extinct group of sphagesaurid notosuchians, a lineage of crocodile relatives.
The defining specimen for the type species consists of an almost complete skull, a lower jaw missing only three teeth, and partial body parts.
This animal possesses roughly ten unique physical traits known as autapomorphies that distinguish it from other relatives.
In this species, the opening for the external nostrils is bordered entirely by the premaxillae bones.
Each premaxilla bone contains four teeth arranged in a specific pattern.
A gap called a diastema exists within the premaxillary tooth row and another separates the premaxillary and maxillary teeth.
The lower jaw features ten teeth on each side, separated by two distinct gaps.
The front teeth were shaped for capturing prey, while the rear teeth were adapted for processing food.

The species C. catanduvensis, described in 2024, features a distinct internal chamber linked to airways that may have been used for vocalization; specimens were discovered in the municipality of Catanduva, northern São Paulo, from the Adamantina Formation.
The species C. attenboroughi was named in 2021 to honor the renowned naturalist David Attenborough, based on remains from the Aptian-Campanian strata of the Santo Anastácio Formation.
The genus was first described by Iori and Carvalho in 2011.
The type species C. paulistanus received its name in that same year.
The holotype specimen was found on the São Francisco Farm in Monte Alto County, northern São Paulo.
The species C. montealtensis was moved to this genus in 2013, having originally been named Sphagesaurus montealtensis in 2008.
Another species, C. stenognathus, was formally described in 2014.
A third species, C. mineirus, was described in 2018.
This genus belongs to the parent group Caipirasuchinae.
It is classified within the family Sphagesauridae.
Fossils of this animal date to the Late Cretaceous period.
Caipirasuchus lived between 93.9 and 66 million years ago, spanning from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian.
Remains have been found in northern São Paulo State and western Minas Gerais State in southeastern Brazil.
The holotype was collected from the Adamantina Formation of the Bauru Basin, dating to the Turonian and Santonian stages.
Specimens of C. catanduvensis were discovered in the municipality of Catanduva, northern São Paulo, from the Adamantina Formation.
